Crash.type: Compiler crash (internal error in IPA mod-ref analysis, ealias pass)
Crash.explanation: Three nested functions inside one function, the first carrying a section attribute and called by the third, trip a gcc_checking_assert in gimple_call_static_chain_flags (gimple.cc:1683, 'nested functions should always bind to current def') during the ealias pass at -O1 and above; -O0 compiles cleanly. This is a different failure site than a nested-function lowering crash in tree-nested.cc: the compiler survives lowering and fails later in IPA mod-ref analysis. Program is GNU C (nested functions); clang rejects the extension by design, GCC-only construct.

reproduce.expected: The file compiles successfully (as it does at -O0).
reproduce.observed:
internal compiler error: in gimple_call_static_chain_flags, at gimple.cc:1683
Reproduces at -O1/-O2/-O3/-Os (not -O0/-Og).

Crash.type: Compiler crash (internal error in the C front end)
Crash.explanation: A conditional expression whose second operand applies logical negation to a _Float16 expression (!(m + 1)) while the third operand mixes _Float16 arithmetic trips the operand-1 gcc_assert in build_conditional_expr, at c/c-typeck.cc:5714. This is the sibling assertion of the previously seen operand-2 failure at line 5720 (same excess-precision handling, opposite operand position), reached at every optimization level. The program is valid: clang-19.1.7 accepts it cleanly (-std=c23, -fsyntax-only).

reproduce.observed:
internal compiler error: in build_conditional_expr, at c/c-typeck.cc:5714
Reproduces at every optimization level (-O0/-O1/-O2/-O3).

Crash.type: Compiler crash (internal error in constant folding, C++ front end)
Crash.explanation: A constexpr aggregate initialized with a pointer-to-member-function converted across virtual inheritance (static_cast<fn_t>(&Derived::doit) with 'struct Derived : virtual Base') aborts the C++ front end in fold_convert_loc (fold-const.cc:2757) at any optimization level. Same failure site as the non-virtual-inheritance case, reached through a different conversion shape. clang++-19 rejects the program (stricter constexpr member-pointer rules); for GCC it is at minimum a crash-on-invalid robustness failure — the compiler should diagnose, not ICE.

reproduce.observed:
internal compiler error: in fold_convert_loc, at fold-const.cc:2757
Reproduces at every optimization level (-O0/-O1/-O2/-O3).

Crash.type: Compiler crash (internal error in C++ name mangling)
Crash.explanation: A requires-clause on a member function of a nested local struct inside a template, referencing sizeof of a function-local static constexpr array, crashes GCC 14.3.0 in the name mangler: discriminator_for_local_entity (cp/mangle.cc:2264) hits gcc_checking_assert(DECL_ARTIFICIAL(entity)) on an entity with no lang-specific data. Reproduces at every optimization level with -std=c++20. (The same function has a known sibling report PR123529 at line 2316, which is RESOLVED; this line-2264 assertion survives that fix.) The program is valid C++20: clang++-19 accepts it cleanly; the ICE is in name mangling, not instantiation.

reproduce.observed:
internal compiler error: in discriminator_for_local_entity, at cp/mangle.cc:2264
Reproduces at every optimization level (-O0/-O1/-O2/-O3).

Miscompilation.type: Miscompilation (asm goto with memory output operands; silent wrong value)
Miscompilation.explanation: asm goto with '+m' output operands and a thread_local memory input is miscompiled by GCC 14.3.0 on the label path: test(1) must return saved-1 = -1, but the generated code returns 0 at -O0/-O1 and 1 at -O2/-O3. No crash — a silent wrong value whose value itself depends on the optimization level, while clang 19.1.0 compiles the same source correctly at every level and the source is UBSan-clean. (Also reproduces on GCC 13.1: a longstanding asm-goto output-operand issue, i.e. a different manifestation than the -O1-only control-flow-merge crash family.) UBSan-clean (clang-19.1.7 -fsanitize=undefined -O0): no runtime errors; the miscompile is confirmed against clang as reference.

reproduce.expected: The program prints "normal=1" then "abort=-1" (as clang 19.1.0 does at every optimization level).
reproduce.observed: -O0 and -O1 builds print "abort=0"; -O2 and -O3 builds print "abort=1"; none prints the correct -1.

Crash.type: Compiler crash (Clang front end, during IR generation)
Crash.explanation: A class template that additionally declares an alias template over its nested dependent type (template<class U> using Alias = typename Inner::T2;) crashes Clang 19.1.0 when a function whose return type is the dependent nested alias without typename is instantiated: ASTContext::getTypeInfoImpl reaches an undeduced type. Crashes even on an assertions-off build. Alternative reproducer of the same getTypeInfoImpl failure. The program is valid: g++-13 accepts it cleanly; Clang crashes instead of compiling it.

reproduce.expected: The file compiles successfully (it is valid C++17).
reproduce.observed: The compiler crashes with a stack dump while generating IR for the instantiated function (DenseMap<Type const*, TypeInfo> lookup on an undeduced type).

Crash.explanation: A function-local static declared inside a lambda nested in a template function, bound to a reference non-type template parameter, crashes Clang 19.1.0 in code generation: the Expr-to-Value DenseMap corrupts (DenseMap<const clang::Expr*, llvm::Value*>::moveFromOldBuckets via CrashRecoveryContext). The same pattern without the intervening lambda crashes earlier in Sema instantiation instead — the lambda reroutes the failure into CodeGen, a different crash site. The program is valid: g++-13 accepts it cleanly; Clang crashes in CodeGen.

reproduce.observed: The compiler crashes with a stack dump whose top frames are in llvm::DenseMapBase<... clang::Expr const*, llvm::Value* ...>::moveFromOldBuckets during CodeGen (caught by the crash recovery handler).

Crash.type: Compiler crash (Clang front end, expression classification)
Crash.explanation: A trailing return type that instantiates a constant-wrapper template whose stored callable is a multiplication functor crashes Clang 19.1.0 in ClassifyInternal (clang/lib/AST/ExprClassification.cpp:339) during auto return-type deduction. Same classification failure as the addition-functor case, reached with a different callable. The program is valid: g++-13 accepts it cleanly.

reproduce.observed: Segmentation fault: expression classification (ClassifyInternal) dereferences an invalid state while instantiating the constant wrapper in the trailing return type.

Crash.type: Compiler crash (Clang front end, deduction-guide instantiation)
Crash.explanation: A deduction guide on an inner class template whose target is decltype(sizeof...(Args)) of the outer parameter pack crashes Clang 19.1.0 while the guide is instantiated (TemplateInstantiator::TransformType), at any optimization level. g++-13 rejects the deduction-guide form (stricter front end); the Clang crash is at minimum a robustness failure (should diagnose, not crash).

reproduce.observed: The compiler crashes with a stack dump while instantiating the inner class template's deduction guide (at any optimization level, -O0 through -O3).

Miscompilation.type: Miscompilation (generated program crashes at runtime, -O1 only)
Miscompilation.explanation: Clang 19.1.0 -O1 mis-compiles this switch/loop program (7-element array, cases 0/3 in the infinite-loop guard switch) so the binary segfaults; -O0/-O2/-O3 are correct and the source is UBSan-clean (clang-19.1.7 -fsanitize=undefined at -O0). Same -O1-only runtime-crash family, different program constants and control-flow values. UBSan-clean (clang-19.1.7 -fsanitize=undefined -O0).

reproduce.expected: Correct behavior: the program simply returns (exit 0). This is what the -O0, -O2 and -O3 builds do, and the source is free of undefined behavior.
reproduce.observed: Only the -O1 build is affected: the resulting binary dies with SIGSEGV right at start (exit 139).

Miscompilation.type: Miscompilation (x86-64 backend: shift+mask equality compiled as a non-equivalent rotate, _BitInt(13))
Miscompilation.explanation: Clang 19.1.0 for x86-64 compiles (v << 2) == (v & -4) on a 13-bit integer as a rotate comparison, giving wrong answers for inputs a=2730 and a=5461 at -O1/-O2 (-O0 is correct; UBSan-clean). The 3-bit case generalizes: the wrong fold fires whenever the shift amount does not divide the bit width. An i13 IR-level reproducer is included; the same wrong fold is visible when test11.ll is compiled with llc for x86-64. Also reproduces on clang 19.1.7. UBSan-clean; the same wrong fold reproduces on clang 19.1.7, and the i13 IR-level reproducer mismatches under llc on exactly the same two inputs.

reproduce.environment: Clang 19.1.0 (x86-64-unknown-linux-gnu); llc 19.1.0 for the IR-level reproducer
reproduce.command: clang -O1 test11.c -o a.out && ./a.out   # also -O2; IR level: llc -mtriple=x86_64-linux-gnu -filetype=obj test11.ll && link test11_driver.c
reproduce.expected: Every input a in 0..8191 must match the reference computed in 64-bit arithmetic (the -O0 build prints "RESULT: correct").
reproduce.observed: -O1/-O2 builds print "a=2730 got=3 exp=1" and "a=5461 got=3 exp=1", then "RESULT: wrong 2". The generated code compares X against rotl(X, 2) instead of evaluating (X << 2) == (X & -4) on the 13-bit value. The llc-compiled IR reproducer mismatches on exactly the same two inputs.

Miscompilation.type: Miscompilation (SLP vectorizer narrows a comparison; silent wrong value)
Miscompilation.explanation: Stride variant of the SLP-narrowing miscompile: with loop strides i += 3, j += 1 over the 6x6 array, Clang 19.1.0 -O2/-O3 SLP-vectorizes the unsigned-short comparison as a signed 16-bit compare and prints acc=0 instead of acc=12; -O0/-O1 are correct, GCC 13.1 -O2 is correct, and the source is UBSan-clean. UBSan-clean; GCC 13.1 -O2 computes the correct value (12).

reproduce.expected: The program prints "acc=12 (expected 12)" (as the -O0 and -O1 builds do).
reproduce.observed: The -O2/-O3 builds print "acc=0 (expected 12)". No crash — the value is silently wrong.
